messages:
Anna R.: Heads-up — org-wide cutover next month: we are retiring legacy OAuth apps for CI/deploy integrations and migrating to GitHub Apps + OIDC-based short-lived tokens. Timeline: sandbox testing starts Mon 2026-04-06, staged rollout Apr 13–20, org enforcement Apr 21.

Mike L.: Nice — high level: will this break existing deploy keys or self-hosted runners?

Anna R.: Short answer: no forced downtime. We’ll create GitHub Apps for each service and a migration shim that exchanges OAuth tokens for app installations. Self-hosted runners unaffected, but any CI jobs that rely on org-scoped OAuth tokens will need an update to use the new app credentials or OIDC.

Sarah K.: Where do we test? Link to sandbox org?

Anna R.: Test in the `redwood-sandbox` org (invite sent). Docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/docs/github-app-migration. Please run the checklist in the doc and open a migration ticket if you hit issues.

Ben (security): Important: as part of this cutover we will enable the OAuth App allowlist and enforce GitHub App-only for org-level integrations. Exceptions only with SIRT approval. Also rotating all long-lived deploy keys is part of the plan.

Jules P.: Do we have a migration script? Can it be used by teams with custom scripts?

Anna R.: Yes — there's a migration CLI: `rw-github-migrate`. Example usage:```bash
# migrate repo-level oauth token to app
rw-github-migrate --repo redwood/ingress --from-token $LEGACY_TOKEN --install-id 12345
``` It will create an install, copy required perms, and print a compatibility shim you can drop into CI.

Mike L.: Will `rw-github-migrate` run in CI or do we run locally?

Anna R.: You can run it locally or from a temporary job in CI. We’ll offer a hosted migration endpoint for teams that prefer we run it.

Infra-bot: Reminder: automated dependency scan scheduled for Apr 5 — move any oauth tokens out of repo secrets before that date to avoid false positives.

Sarah K.: What about third-party integrations like Sentry/Datadog that use OAuth?

Ben (security): Those will need a GitHub App integration or an org-approved proxy. We’re coordinating with vendor owners; expect vendor-specific instructions in the doc.

Jules P.: Any breaking changes to webhook payloads or permissions?

Anna R.: Webhook payloads unchanged. Permission granularity increases (we encourage repo-scoped app installs). If you rely on org-level admin scopes, open a ticket — we’ll propose minimal perms.

Mike L.: Who do I @ if my team needs an exception?

Ben (security): Ping me and include use-case, CI job IDs, and why app install isn't feasible. Exception reviews take up to 48 hours.

Ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window reserved: 2026-04-15 02:00–04:00 UTC for org enforcement smoke tests.

Sarah K.: Can we get a quick rollback plan? If something breaks during staged rollout?

Anna R.: Yes — rollback is to re-enable previous OAuth token policy for affected repos and open a hotfix ticket. We’ll keep a fallback window for 48 hours after each staged batch.

Mike L.: Thx. We'll sign up for the Apr 13 batch.

Anna R.: Great — sign-up form: https://go.redwood.dev/github-app-cutover. Please complete by Apr 3.

Ben (security): Also: rotate service-account keys by Apr 10. We’ll publish a rotation guide with `gcloud` / `aws` examples.

Jules P.: Noted. I’ll coordinate with infra to ensure our terraform modules support app installs.

Anna R.: Thanks all — will post daily status updates in this thread during rollout. :rocket:
